finalMessage:
Both changes are done and the checks pass. You can now name a game before saving it, and the name comes back when you load that save. Saves that wouldn't open after pasting now load. Nothing is committed.

**Why pasted saves failed.** The loader required `version` to be the first key in the save. Your own exports always put it first, so they loaded. A save that had been through a JSON formatter or another tool usually has its keys in a different order, and it was rejected as "Invalid snapshot." even though nothing in it was wrong. The loader in `src/game/snapshot.ts` now accepts the fields in whatever order they come. Everything else is still checked the same way: each field must appear exactly once, no extra fields are allowed, and the version, size limit and game-state rules are unchanged.

**Naming a game.**
- There is a new "Game name" field in the Reproduce a game panel, above Snapshot JSON, limited to 60 characters.
- Export snapshot writes the name into the save, and Load snapshot puts it back in the field.
- New Game and Load board start a game with no name, and Restart keeps the current name.
- An unnamed export is exactly the same as before: there is no `name` field, the version stays 1, and the replay command's output is unchanged.
- A save with a name won't open in a copy of the game built before this change, because older builds reject any field they don't know.
- When loading, spaces around a name are trimmed and an empty name means unnamed. A name that isn't text, is over 60 characters or contains control characters such as a line break makes the save invalid.

The name rules are in the new file `src/game/game-name.ts`. The session keeps the name in `src/game/session/session.ts` and `use-game.ts`. The field is in `src/game/controls/Reproduction.tsx`, with its label in `control-labels.ts` and its style in `reproduction.css`, and `src/game/Game.tsx` connects them. I also added a line about naming and pasted saves to the README's play section.

**Project rules.** I followed the rules the project's own checks enforce: files of 200 lines or fewer, no forbidden words or type casts, every export used somewhere, test names without requirement IDs, and spacing values on the project's scale.

**Tests added.**
- `src/game/game-name.test.ts`: saving and loading a name, unnamed saves, fields in other orders, and invalid names.
- A test in `src/game/session/session.test.ts` for when the name is kept or cleared.
- A browser test in `tests/snapshots.e2e.test.ts` that names a game, exports it, starts a new game, loads the save back, and then loads it again with its fields reversed.

I also confirmed that the old loader rejected a save with its fields reordered.

**Check results.**
- `npm run typecheck` passes, and `npm test` passes all 147 tests.
- `npm run test:e2e` passes all 78 browser tests. This ran on Node 22.23.4 and npm 10.9.9 rather than the README's named versions (Playwright and Chromium did match), so it doesn't count as evidence for the named combination. To get it into the project folder, I downloaded Chromium 156.0.8078.4 to `.playwright-browsers/`, which git ignores.
- `npm run format:check` reports 3 files: `scripts/replay.test.ts`, `tests/accessibility.e2e.test.ts` and `tests/layout.e2e.test.ts`. They fail the same way without my changes, I didn't edit them, and every file I changed is formatted correctly.

The project is at `the project`.

Both changes are in: you can now name a game before saving it, and the name comes back when you load that save. Saves you paste now open even when their fields are in a different order from my exports. All checks pass: type check, 146 unit tests and 79 browser tests. Nothing is committed.

I followed the project rules. The `open-forge` CLI isn't installed, so I read the loader, its required catalogues and `docs/README.md` with its linked specs by hand. The specs already define both behaviours (Controls C15, Reproducibility D05/D06), so I changed no spec files.

**Why pasted saves failed**
The import code required `version` to be the first field. The spec doesn't require any field order. So a save whose fields had been reordered, for example sorted alphabetically by another tool, was rejected. I checked this against the original code: the same save with sorted fields was rejected, and with `version` first it loaded. Import now checks only that each field is present exactly once, in any order. All the other validation is unchanged.

**Deal names**
- **Field:** a "Deal name" text input in the "Reproduce a game" panel. It starts empty and allows up to 40 characters (counted as UTF-16 code units). Line breaks are rejected; spaces and all other characters are kept as typed. Editing it leaves cards, moves, the clock and any pause unchanged, including while paused or after a win.
- **Export:** a named game exports as version 2 with a `name` field. An unnamed game still exports as version 1, and the replay command still outputs version 1.
- **Import:**
  - A named save restores its name, and an unfinished one loads paused until you select Resume.
  - A completed named save keeps the static win banner and doesn't change the best score.
  - A version 1 save clears the name.
  - Version 2 without a valid name, a name in a version 1 save, or any other version is rejected.
- **Clearing:** New Game, Restart, changing size, loading a board code and reloading the page all clear the name. Names aren't stored in browser preferences.

**Files**
- New: `src/game/deal-name.ts` holds the 40-character limit and the name check.
- `src/game/game.ts`: game state has a `name` field, empty for an unnamed game.
- `src/game/snapshot.ts`: the version 2 format and the field-order fix.
- `src/game/session/session.ts` and `src/game/session/use-game.ts`: renaming the game.
- UI: `src/game/controls/Reproduction.tsx`, `src/game/controls/control-labels.ts`, `src/game/controls/reproduction.css` and `src/game/Game.tsx`.
- New tests: `src/game/named-snapshot.test.ts` and `tests/deal-name.e2e.test.ts`. I also added a rename test to `src/game/session/session.test.ts`.
- I updated `README.md`: status is now spec version 3, with the new behaviour and an accurate test record.

**Before you rely on the test record**
- This machine has Node 22.23.4 and npm 10.9.9, which is below the project's minimum of Node 24.19. I installed Playwright's Chromium 156.0.8078.4 into `.playwright-browsers/`, which git ignores. The README now says these spec version 3 changes have no record on the project's reference Node/npm/Playwright versions yet. That run is still needed.
- The formatting check already reported 23 files before I started, mostly under `docs/` and `.agents/`. I left them alone; every file I changed passes it.

Nothing needed saving to the project's notes folder (`.agents/memory`).

Both changes are done: you can now name a game before you save it, and the name comes back when you load the save. Saves that you paste in now open even when their fields are in a different order. I ran the type check, the unit tests (146) and the full browser suite (79 journeys, including 2 new ones) on Node 24.22.1 and npm 11.19.1 with Playwright 1.64.1 and Chromium 156.0.8078.4, and they all pass. I didn't run them on the project's named combination (Node 26.12.1 / npm 11.20.0), because that Node version isn't installed here. `npm run format:check` was already failing before I started, on all ten `docs/` files and three existing test files; my files pass it, and I left those files alone. Nothing is committed.

**Why pasted saves wouldn't open.** In `src/game/snapshot.ts`, the loader required `"version"` to be the first field in the JSON. Your own exports always put it first, so they worked. A save that went through another tool or editor that reorders or sorts the fields was rejected, even though the spec says nothing about field order. The loader now accepts the fields in any order but still requires exactly the right set of them. Tests cover sorted and reversed field order for both save versions, and a browser journey loads a reversed save that is indented differently.

**Deal name**, following `docs/controls.md` C15 and `docs/reproducibility.md` D05:
- **The field:** a "Deal name" text box inside "Reproduce a game". It starts empty and allows up to 40 characters on one line. Spaces around the name are kept exactly as typed, and clearing the box makes the game unnamed. You can rename while the game is paused or finished, and renaming doesn't change the board, moves, clock or pause.
- **Saving:** a named game exports as a version 2 snapshot that includes the name, and an unnamed game still exports version 1.
- **Loading:** a version 2 save brings back its name with the usual pause and Resume. A finished named save stays still and doesn't change your best score. Loading a version 1 save clears the name.
- **When the name clears:** New Game, Restart, changing the grid size, Load board and reloading the page. Names are never stored in the browser's saved preferences.
- **Replay:** the command-line tool still prints unnamed version 1 snapshots.

**What changed:**
- New files:
  - `src/game/deal-name.ts`: the name rules.
  - `src/game/controls/DealNameField.tsx` and `src/game/controls/deal-name.css`: the field and its styling.
  - `src/game/named-snapshot.test.ts` and `tests/deal-name.e2e.test.ts`: the new tests.
- Changed:
  - `src/game/snapshot.ts`: the two save versions and the field-order fix.
  - `src/game/game.ts`: game state now carries a `name`, empty when unnamed.
  - `src/game/session/session.ts` and `use-game.ts`: renaming.
  - `src/game/controls/Reproduction.tsx`, `control-labels.ts` and `src/game/Game.tsx`: wiring and the label.
  - `src/game/game.fixture.ts`: the expected values from the spec.
  - `src/game/session/session.test.ts`: a new renaming test.
- `README.md`: the status now says it implements spec version 3, the Play section describes deal names, and the test record says what ran for this version, including that the named combination wasn't rerun.
